success_story_description: Renuo AG wanted cloud hosting without the detours. With Deploio, they found the perfect Swiss Heroku alternative – simple, sovereign, carefree.
success_story_long_description: Renuo AG is a Swiss software engineering company with a mission: to write great code – preferably in Ruby on Rails – without having to deal with server administration. For years, everything ran via Heroku, until a single Slack message got everything rolling. In this success story, we tell you how Renuo found the perfect cloud hosting partner in Switzerland – and why Deploio is now the clear number one for them.
success_story_before_cloud_text: Deploio is operated by Nine and we used to be a Nine customer. That was before the cloud. We set up and operated servers for our customers. That took a lot of time and nerves: Buying SSL certificates, managing SSH access, monitoring disk space, updating system libraries. But then came Heroku. It freed us from server administration. We were able to concentrate on software development, even without vendor lock-in thanks to 12factor. Simply “git push”, CI/CD and the customer can test. So we moved to the cloud.
success_story_beauty_and_the_beast_text: Renuo is an owner-managed Swiss company. But Heroku is American and runs on AWS. That bothered us for the next ten years. It must be possible to use a product as cool as Heroku in Switzerland, where I can kick down doors if I don't like something – good luck with that at Salesforce. We were in the Enterprise contract; simply a construct from hell. That's when Deploio came to the rescue and at the right time!
success_story_note_title: We code, Deploio does the rest
success_story_note_text: We are in the software business, not the infrastructure business. I don't want to run Kubernetes myself or bare-metal servers (how do I separate clients? who actually does kernel updates?). We develop good code, that must be enough: 'git push', CI/CD and the customer can test. Deploio handles the infrastructure, in Switzerland, and they do it well. I never had to break down the door at Stauffacher Square.
success_story_slack_message_1_text: Hey everyone. Is anyone primarily hosting with Heroku and also not happy with their recently announced changes? It would be a good opportunity to set up something of our own. I look forward to receiving PMs.
success_story_slack_message_2_text:
Hey Samuel
We're not using Heroku ourselves, but we have a lot of our own infrastructure, a Kubernetes platform in our own datacenter, and a platform based on Google's Kubernetes Engine on Google Cloud.
What exactly do you want to do? What don't you like about Heroku?
Maybe we should talk?
Regards
Tom
Oh... we/I = nine.ch
success_story_note_quote: Cloud yes, but preferably in Switzerland from a Swiss company with capable engineers, not just Amazon resellers.
success_story_demokratis_description: Demokratis wants to digitalize Swiss politics. In Deploio, they found a local partner – secure, reliable, and uncomplicated.
success_story_demokratis_long_descriptio: Bringing Swiss politics into the digital age is no walk in the park. Especially not when cantons and public authorities are the primary customers. Because when it comes to sensitive data and server locations, the fun stops. In this success story, we share how the independent platform Demokratis found the perfect Swiss cloud solution with Deploio – and why it makes a massive difference when a partner offers flexible help right where it hurts the most.
success_story_demokratis_public_hand_tit: THE CHALLENGE WITH THE PUBLIC SECTOR
success_story_demokratis_public_hand_tex:
For Demokratis's customers and partners, who primarily come from the public sector (such as cantons), the data location is absolutely essential. A solution hosted abroad?
That is simply out of the question for these governmental processes.

In addition, there was a real technical nut to crack: the first cantons are using the Demokratis application under their own domains. This required setting up CNAME records that seamlessly forward to the Demokratis platform. For the migration, they needed a partner capable of reliably handling this specific domain routing.
success_story_demokratis_swissness_text: The solution? "Demokratis powered by Deploio". Moving was the logical step to meet the strict requirements of the authorities. The main reason for the migration was obvious: the entire infrastructure is located in Switzerland and is provided and managed by Deploio. This gives the cantons the necessary security and trust.
success_story_demokratis_note_text:
We aren't hardcore techies. That's why we broke a bit of a sweat during the complete cloud setup and migration of our platform. But instead of anonymous ticket systems, we received super flexible support directly via Slack and personal emails. We needed a few special features for the routing – and the Deploio team delivered them for us quickly and without any fuss. It’s just cool to be so close to the product.

On top of that, we now have modern deployments. Deploying a feature branch via nctl as a staging app, testing it, and you're done. We can focus entirely on our mission and make public consultations more inclusive. Deploio handles the infrastructure for it, securely and completely in Switzerland. And they do a really good job at it.
success_story_demokratis_quote_text: Our mission is digital democracy, not server management. With Deploio’s PaaS solution, we don’t have to worry about the infrastructure at all.
success_story_swissict_description: When the previous hosting partner of the swissICT salary survey ceased operations, only a few weeks remained to find a new solution. With Deploio, it now runs on Swiss infrastructure, under Swiss law, using a fifth of the original server resources.
success_story_swissict_long_description: With its salary survey, swissICT has for years delivered the largest and most independent study of the Swiss IT working world – a key reference for HR and recruiting across the country. Hosting ran smoothly for years, until the previous partner unexpectedly ceased operations in 2024. In this success story, we share how swissICT found a Swiss partner that takes data sovereignty seriously within just a few weeks – and why the salary survey runs on Deploio today.
success_story_swissict_challenge_text:
In 2024, the salary survey's previous development and hosting partner ceased operations. A new solution had to be found within a few weeks. As the study grows in relevance and compliance requirements increase significantly, so do the demands on every partner involved in the project.

The central question goes beyond mere control: which service providers are trustworthy enough to safeguard data sovereignty? How do partners ensure that compliance-relevant processes are transparent and legally compliant? Where exactly is the data hosted – and under what conditions? One thing is clear: improvised back-room hosting is not an option, and neither is one-sided dependence on global US corporations.
success_story_swissict_solution_title: DATA SOVEREIGNTY AS A DECISIVE FACTOR
success_story_swissict_solution_text: The choice fell on Deploio, the Swiss app engine for web agencies and organizations that value digital sovereignty. The PaaS solution offers modern deployment standards, full data sovereignty and a clear cost structure, operated in an ISO 27001-certified data centre in Zurich. Unlike global cloud providers that do run servers in Switzerland but are subject to the US Cloud Act, Deploio guarantees that sensitive data never leaves the country. For swissICT this was a decisive criterion: true digital sovereignty means not only a location in Zurich, but also legal independence.
success_story_swissict_note_text:
At the same time, Deploio convinces with its practical architecture. The platform provides a ready-to-use environment with common frameworks, databases and development tools – without ballast, and without having to manage operating systems or infrastructure yourself: link the GitHub repository to Deploio, and you're done.

That left the technical service provider behind the salary survey free to focus on what mattered: a secure and fast migration. Thanks to Deploio's automated workflows – from testing to rolling out new versions – the transition worked smoothly from day one and was completed on schedule despite the tight timeline.

OK – admittedly – it didn't go quite that smoothly: because the app had been provisioned with 16 GB of RAM in the old setup, a few performance improvements were needed. Today the same app runs on 2 GB of RAM. And the 2025 salary survey was carried out successfully. All's well that ends well.
success_story_swissict_quote_text: The migration of the salary survey succeeded in early 2025 and proved that digital sovereignty is achievable. In swissICT's case, it required a deliberate decision to take the safe route with local partner companies.
